claims.claim: End-to-end exactly-once business effects cannot be guaranteed by a workflow runtime alone; require target-side idempotency/dedup
claims.counterevidence: none found; vendor claims are all boundary-scoped
claims.boundary: proven for systems that cannot observe target state
claims.hf_consequence: HF contracts must never claim unscoped effect exactly-once
claims.falsifier: durable runtime demonstrating exactly-once effects on arbitrary non-idempotent external API

claims.claim: Absence of a success acknowledgement is not evidence of failure
claims.counterevidence: distinction collapses for naturally idempotent effects (harmless to retry)
claims.hf_consequence: mandate UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; forbid timeout=failed
claims.falsifier: method distinguishing message-loss from execution-failure at distance with zero extra round-trips

claims.claim: Source-native atomic conditional mutation superior to harness read-check-write for source-local invariants
claims.counterevidence: DynamoDB global tables LWW breaks optimistic locking; HTTP date validators 1-second granularity; conditional writes do not dedupe retries by themselves
claims.hf_consequence: Rule R2; ban harness read-check-write on guarded resources
claims.falsifier: source-local invariant a harness check enforces more strongly than the source's conditional write

claims.claim: A distributed lock does not protect a resource that does not itself reject stale holders; fencing requires resource cooperation
claims.counterevidence: antirez: bounded clocks suffice for efficiency-class locks
claims.hf_consequence: no locks as safety mechanisms for external effects; prefer conditional writes
claims.falsifier: lock-only system with demonstrated stale-holder safety vs unbounded pauses and no resource-side checks

claims.claim: Compensation is a new business operation, not a technical rollback; can fail or be impossible
claims.counterevidence: LLM-generated compensation is research-grade only
claims.boundary: semantic business reversal; DB rollbacks are a different mechanism
claims.hf_consequence: compensation as domain op with identity/authorization/idempotency; never auto-inverse
claims.falsifier: generic automatic inverse safe across heterogeneous business systems

claims.claim: Event sourcing is neither necessary for durable execution/audit nor sufficient as an audit log
claims.counterevidence: ES does provide change history within one trust domain; temporal queries are ES-strength
claims.hf_consequence: ES activation conditions only; default = transactional state + append-only audit/receipts
claims.falsifier: compliance regime accepting vanilla event stores as sufficient legal audit evidence without integrity anchoring

claims.claim: 'Exactly-once' vendor claims are boundary-specific and frequently misread
claims.counterevidence: none; vendors scope their own claims
claims.hf_consequence: glossary fixes delivery/processing/effect suffixes; bans unscoped usage
claims.falsifier: vendor doc claiming unscoped end-to-end effect exactly-once

claims.claim: Stable effect identity required only for a subset of effects (harmful non-idempotent class)
claims.counterevidence: universal keying is harmless but not necessary; keys can mislead when identity is wrong
claims.hf_consequence: effect-class-driven identity requirement
claims.falsifier: read-only effect requiring identity for correctness (not analytics)

claims.claim: Delayed duplicates beyond native dedup windows occur and are material for harmful effects
claims.counterevidence: none claiming windows cover all duplicate horizons
claims.hf_consequence: dedup horizon = business-defined; exceed native windows where harm is material
claims.falsifier: native provider guaranteeing unbounded dedup retention

claims.claim: Durable runtimes re-execute activities/steps after crash-before-record; external calls need identity guards
claims.counterevidence: at-most-once modes exist but trade skips for duplicates
claims.boundary: at-most-once is per attempt, not per workflow
claims.hf_consequence: identity-before-attempt ordering; receipts after
claims.falsifier: runtime that checkpoints before external calls and never replays them (still fails lost acks)

claims.claim: Orchestrator/replay code containing direct external effects is a correctness defect
claims.counterevidence: none
claims.hf_consequence: separate plan/decide (pure) from act (guarded); zero external calls in replayed logic
claims.falsifier: replay-based engine safely tolerating nondeterministic external calls in replayed logic

claims.claim: Leases require clock/rate assumptions and admit dual holders during skew; fencing closes it only at token-checking resources
claims.counterevidence: antirez: bounded clocks suffice for efficiency purposes
claims.hf_consequence: lease usage restricted to HF-internal authority; fencing only where token checks exist
claims.falsifier: lease protocol with proven no-dual-holder property under arbitrary skew without resource checks

claims.claim: Native dedup windows + fingerprints conflict with legitimate re-planning (same logical effect, changed payload)
claims.counterevidence: Stripe recommends fresh keys when modifying a request — new logical effect; boundary is a business call
claims.boundary: depends on HF logical-effect identity definition under replanning
claims.hf_consequence: define identity stability rules for re-planned operations (OQ-3)
claims.falsifier: general rule classifying payload changes as same/new effect without business input

claims.claim: HF-owned machinery can reduce reliability when the source has stronger native guarantees
claims.counterevidence: sources without native guards need harness machinery; harness records still needed for evidence
claims.boundary: preference, not elimination; holds only where native mechanism provably expresses the invariant
claims.hf_consequence: source-native gate in promotion process
claims.falsifier: invariant class where harness-side implementation dominates all native options

claims.claim: 2PC-class distributed transactions are a poor fit as an HF coordination mechanism
claims.counterevidence: XA viable in closed single-org database fleets
claims.boundary: heterogeneous external APIs cannot participate in 2PC at all
claims.hf_consequence: design for local atomicity + compensation/reconciliation, not distributed transactions
claims.falsifier: wide adoption of XA-style coordination across arbitrary SaaS APIs

claims.claim: Pub/Sub 'exactly-once delivery' = no-redelivery-after-ack, not exactly-once processing
claims.counterevidence: none
claims.hf_consequence: terminology entry; no processing guarantees inferred
claims.falsifier: Google documentation extending guarantee to downstream processing

claims.claim: SQS FIFO dedup ≠ consumer idempotency (send-side, windowed)
claims.counterevidence: none
claims.hf_consequence: effect-level dedup not inherited from queue dedup
claims.falsifier: AWS docs guaranteeing consumer-side dedup via MessageDeduplicationId

claims.claim: Step Functions Standard 'exactly-once execution model' refers to workflow/task starts by the service; coexists with retry-driven re-execution; Express is at-least-once
claims.counterevidence: none (vendor self-consistent)
claims.boundary: scoped to Step Functions execution semantics
claims.hf_consequence: evidence for terminology gate
claims.falsifier: vendor doc unifying execution-model and external-effect guarantees

claims.claim: HF can rely on provider webhooks as sole truth for outcome resolution
claims.counterevidence: webhook delivery itself is at-least-once, unordered, can be missed
claims.boundary: webhooks are evidence inputs, never sole authority
claims.hf_consequence: reconciliation = query + webhook + receipts with polling fallback
claims.falsifier: provider guaranteeing transactional, ordered, lossless webhook delivery

claims.claim: Checkpoint+journal history is sufficient internal state machinery for HF workflow durability; full ES adds capability only under named activation conditions
claims.counterevidence: ES value where temporal-query requirements exist
claims.boundary: HF-internal state vs business-domain event streams
claims.hf_consequence: default HF state model = transactional state + append-only journal/receipts
claims.falsifier: HF requirement only satisfiable via temporal state reconstruction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Durable workflow execution does not imply exactly-once external business effects
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: at-most-once policies trade duplicates for skips
hypotheses.falsifier: demonstrated effect exactly-once from runtime durability alone

hypotheses.hypothesis: Source-native atomic conditional mutation preferable to external read-check-write for source-local invariants
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: global-table LWW caveat; validator granularity; does not dedupe retries
hypotheses.falsifier: harness check provably stronger than native guard for a source-local invariant

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unknown outcome should be represented explicitly rather than collapsed into success or failure
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: read-only effects do not need the state
hypotheses.falsifier: method always resolving outcome at first failure detection with zero ambiguity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Blind retry unsafe when previous outcome unknown and duplicate execution materially harmful
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: retry with stable identity or native key is the safe form; naturally idempotent effects exempt

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stable effect identity necessary only for selected effect classes
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: universal keying harmless but unnecessary; wrong identity misleads
hypotheses.falsifier: read-only effect requiring identity for correctness

hypotheses.hypothesis: Distributed lock without fencing may fail to prevent stale writers
hypotheses.falsifier: lock-only system safe under unbounded pauses without resource checks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compensation is a separate domain operation rather than a technical rollback
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: DB rollbacks are a different in-system mechanism
hypotheses.falsifier: generic safe auto-inverse across business systems

hypotheses.hypothesis: Event Sourcing not required for every durable or auditable harness
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: ES valuable under temporal-query/rebuild activation conditions
hypotheses.falsifier: HF requirement class only satisfiable via ES

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exactly-once terminology overloaded; must be decomposed by boundary
hypotheses.falsifier: vendor/standard defining unscoped end-to-end effect exactly-once

hypotheses.hypothesis: More harness-owned machinery can reduce reliability when authoritative systems expose stronger native guarantees
hypotheses.counterevidence_boundary: holds only where native mechanism expresses the same invariant more strongly; harness evidence records remain necessary
hypotheses.falsifier: invariant where harness-side implementation dominates all native options

counterevidence.counterevidence: payload-hash fingerprints collapse legitimate distinct operations; one operation with changed payload escapes dedup; different request identities for one logical effect (two-tab SetupIntent case)
counterevidence.resolution: effect identity must be chosen at the logical layer; fingerprint conflicts (422/409) need identity stability rules (OQ-3)

counterevidence.target_claim: webhooks can be sole outcome authority
counterevidence.counterevidence: webhook delivery at-least-once, unordered, missable; orphan-recovery jobs recommended
counterevidence.resolution: C19 CONTRADICTED; reconciliation = query + webhook + receipts

counterevidence.counterevidence: GC pause / delay / clock skew admit dual holders; Kubernetes leaderelection explicitly no fencing; antirez concedes lock-avoidance where resources can CAS
counterevidence.resolution: C04 SUPPORTED for correctness-class; locks demoted to efficiency tools

counterevidence.counterevidence: event store ≠ audit log: no third-party verifiability, compaction/scavenging, app-clock timestamps
counterevidence.resolution: audit-grade evidence needs hash-chain + external timestamps regardless of ES

counterevidence.target_claim: native guards make harness machinery unnecessary everywhere
counterevidence.counterevidence: not all sources offer native guards; native windows bounded; native guards do not carry logical-effect identity
counterevidence.resolution: H10 is a preference with named boundary, not elimination

counterevidence.counterevidence: unsendable email class; compensation can fail; compensation of unknown outcomes unsafe
counterevidence.resolution: C05; pivot-last ordering; compensation contracts only on decided-success outcomes

counterevidence.counterevidence: crash-after-external-success re-executes steps in all four studied runtimes

failure_classes.name: Outcome ambiguity
failure_classes.definition: Consequential operation terminated without usable result signal (timeout, connection loss, indeterminate 5xx, lost ack)

failure_classes.name: Lost acknowledgement
failure_classes.definition: Effect may have executed; ack/response provably or possibly lost

failure_classes.name: Stale-state mutation
failure_classes.definition: Mutation applied on state that changed after the read (lost update)

failure_classes.name: Write conflict
failure_classes.definition: Two legitimate writers produce conflicting outcomes

failure_classes.name: Lease loss
failure_classes.definition: Worker's authority expired mid-flight (may or may not know)

failure_classes.name: Stale writer / zombie
failure_classes.definition: Worker acts after authority moved to another worker

failure_classes.name: Partial multi-system effect
failure_classes.definition: Subset of a multi-system operation committed

failure_classes.name: Crash-after-effect / unrecorded effect
failure_classes.definition: External effect committed; local/recorded state does not reflect it

failure_classes.name: Compensation failure
failure_classes.definition: Compensating operation itself fails or is unsafe to run

failure_classes.name: Irreversibility
failure_classes.definition: Effect has no meaningful inverse; deviation permanent without new forward operations

failure_classes.name: Compensation of unknown outcome
failure_classes.definition: Compensation attempted while original outcome unknown (compensate-nothing / double-compensate)

failure_classes.name: Reconciliation failure
failure_classes.definition: Authoritative query unavailable, ambiguous, or conflicting evidence

failure_classes.name: Replay-induced duplication
failure_classes.definition: Replayed control logic re-issues an external effect

failure_taxonomy_note: Six orthogonal dimensions (D1 outcome determinacy, D2 multiplicity, D3 freshness, D4 authority, D5 scope, D6 recoverability); a single incident maps to a set of classes.

failure_scenarios.name: Lost acknowledgement
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: request sent; remote may have executed; no response; wire cannot distinguish lost-before-execution from lost-after-commit
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: timeout => failure => safe to retry or abort
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: effect classification; mark UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; no automatic retry for harmful effects
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: native idempotency key held stable + authoritative status query before compensation
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: status API may lag the write
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: reconcile (query/webhook/settlement) -> decided state; escalate on conflicting evidence

failure_scenarios.name: Duplicate delivery
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: same logical operation arrives twice (redelivery, double-submit, retry storm)
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: dedup at one layer implies effect-level dedup
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: verified natural idempotency, else stable logical-effect identity checked in durable store
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: native key + HF-side durable dedup keyed on logical identity
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: identity inference for semantically-equal payload-different duplicates
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: reconcile; compensate only if reversible and authorized

failure_scenarios.name: Retry after crash (crash after external success, before recording completion)
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: runtime shows attempt incomplete; provider shows or may later show success
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: at-most-once policy for harmful effects + UNKNOWN_OUTCOME
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: identity generated inside checkpointed step / derived from workflow+activity ID; receipt recorded before success
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: reconcile by effect identity; adopt executed outcome rather than re-executing

failure_scenarios.name: Stale read
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: read V at t0; write at t1; value changed in between
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: read-check-write proves anything about t1 state
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: source-native conditional mutation; handle precondition failure
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: transaction at source; monotonic status preconditions
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: none for source-local invariant with native guard; cross-system invariants unprotected
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: refresh -> revalidate -> retry or abort; never force-write

failure_scenarios.name: Concurrent writers
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: two legitimate workers submit conflicting mutations near-simultaneously
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: first/last-wins acceptable; or harness lock made them serial
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: business-level versioning/epochs; approval for conflict class
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: winner legitimacy is a business question
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: loser reconciles against winner; compensates own partial work if authorized

failure_scenarios.name: Lease expiration
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: A's lease expired possibly unnoticed; B active; both may issue effects
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: lease expiry => old holder stops; new holder sole writer
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: post-expiry A actions treated as stale-writer risks; B's writes conditional on source epoch/version
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: fencing/epoch tokens at acceptance point; else drain + conditional-write gatekeeping
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: expiry-to-notice window irreducible; protection must live at the resource
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: B reconciles A's in-flight operations via effect identity registry

failure_scenarios.name: Partial multi-system effect
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: A committed; B did not; no shared transaction
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: single 'transaction failed' status suffices; re-running whole step safe for A
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: pivot-last ordering; compensable-step registry; invariant reordering
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: A's effect may itself be unknown (compound ambiguity)
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: forward-recover B or compensate A per effect classes; never blanket

failure_scenarios.name: Compensation failure
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: compensation more reliable than forward path; compensation retries harmless forever
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: compensation as effect with own identity, idempotency, retry budget; failure raises alert state
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: longer retry horizon than forward path; escalation queue; human authorization
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: escalate to human with evidence bundle

failure_scenarios.name: Irreversible effect
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: class = NON_IDEMPOTENT_IRREVERSIBLE; approval gate; no compensation field
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: forward correction as new authorized business operation

failure_scenarios.name: Replay containing unsafe external side effect
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: replay of orchestration history performs I/O or unrecorded nondeterminism => duplicate I/O
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: workflow durability makes replayed side effects safe
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: external calls only in non-replayed step/activity boundaries; deterministic APIs inside
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: recorded nondeterminism APIs, knowing they still have no exactly-once guarantee
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: history corruption is separate disaster class
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: runtime-level; HF duty is the constraint

failure_scenarios.name: Delayed duplicate beyond window
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: duplicate after provider pruned key / queue window / name retention
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: window expired => operation finished and safe to re-run
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: HF durable dedup keyed by logical effect, retention >= business horizon; monotonic source preconditions
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: unbounded/long-retention identity store; contractual provider dedup
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: storage lifetime vs business horizon; privacy-law tension
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: duplicate detected late -> reconcile + compensate if authorized

failure_scenarios.name: Unknown authoritative state
failure_scenarios.observable_facts: consequential op issued; outcome unknown; no status endpoint or it is down; webhooks absent/missed
failure_scenarios.unsafe_assumption: after T minutes with no evidence, treat as failed
failure_scenarios.minimum_protection: explicit UNKNOWN_OUTCOME persisted with attempt evidence; no auto retry/compensation
failure_scenarios.stronger_optional: multi-source reconciliation with freshness/authority models; deadline escalation
failure_scenarios.residual_uncertainty: may persist indefinitely (reconciliation failure) — permanent visible limbo with owner is correct
failure_scenarios.recovery_route: scheduled reconciliation with backoff; escalation with evidence; human decision

effect_classes.name: READ_ONLY
effect_classes.reconciliation_requirement: none; freshness validation at use site
effect_classes.validation_requirement: freshness check if used for consequential decisions

effect_classes.name: IDEMPOTENT_WRITE
effect_classes.retry_policy: auto-retry with backoff; safe by construction
effect_classes.identity_requirement: request identity for tracing; effect identity not required if reapplication verified no-op

effect_classes.name: GUARDED_WRITE
effect_classes.identity_requirement: REQUIRED: stable logical identity mapped onto native key/precondition
effect_classes.reconciliation_requirement: status query on unknown outcome; duplicate-proofness delegated to source within window
effect_classes.validation_requirement: verify native window >= duplicate horizon else add HF dedup

effect_classes.name: NON_IDEMPOTENT_REVERSIBLE
effect_classes.retry_policy: at-most-once default; retry only under identity guard or after reconcile
effect_classes.identity_requirement: REQUIRED: logical effect identity + durable dedup

effect_classes_note: Proposed v0.1 starting classes; not final HF enums; subject to fault-injection data.

mechanisms.name: no special mechanism
mechanisms.failure_mode: silent lost updates if assumption wrong

mechanisms.name: serialization (HF-local single-writer)
mechanisms.protected_invariant: one worker at a time per HF

mechanisms.name: optimistic concurrency (harness-side)
mechanisms.failure_mode: divergence from source; race vs external writers

mechanisms.name: transaction
mechanisms.protected_invariant: atomic multi-object invariant in one system

mechanisms.name: lock (harness or DLM)
mechanisms.failure_mode: GC pause/delay => dual holders; no resource enforcement
mechanisms.source_support_required: resource must enforce to be safe

mechanisms.name: source-native transactional mechanism (derived rule)
mechanisms.assumptions: source exposes it (status preconditions, conditional writes)

mechanisms_note: No mechanism in this table protects a cross-system invariant; that class requires saga-style compensation or restructured invariants (S5, S39).

recovery_matrix.applicable_state: decided-failure at transport; or guarded unknown
recovery_matrix.preconditions: stable identity/native key; transient error class
recovery_matrix.own_failure_mode: duplicate if identity lost; retry storm

decision_procedure: classify effect; set defaults from effect class
if duplicate_harm=MATERIAL: identity REQUIRED; map to native key; add HF dedup if native window < retention horizon
on failure signal classify: rejected-before-execution vs UNKNOWN (timeouts/5xx/lost-ack => UNKNOWN by default)
UNKNOWN_OUTCOME action order: query authoritative status -> wait webhook within deadline -> identity-guarded retry only if native key held -> escalate; never compensate from UNKNOWN
record receipts at every transition; ack != outcome

DynamoDB.conditional_writes: yes (condition expressions; zero capacity on failed condition)
DynamoDB.caveat: global tables LWW breaks optimistic locking
DynamoDB.fencing: conditional put with monotonic attr can act as fencing

Temporal.idempotency: WF-ID+Activity-ID recommended key; duplicate-reject start policies

Azure_Durable_Functions.execution: at-least-once activities; idempotency required by docs

AWS_Step_Functions.idempotency: execution-name uniqueness (90 days); same-name+same-input => idempotent start
AWS_Step_Functions.execution: Standard exactly-once execution model (scoped); Express at-least-once

AWS_Durable_Execution_SDK.execution: steps at-least-once; AtMostOncePerRetry x no-retry => exactly-once end-to-end per attempt semantics

decision_rules.rule: IF source offers caller-supplied idempotency keys THEN map HF logical-effect identity onto that key UNLESS native retention window < business duplicate horizon (then add HF dedup too, R6)
decision_rules.activation_condition: consequential effect on source with native keys
decision_rules.residual_risk: window expiry (F11); payload conflict on re-planned ops

decision_rules.rule: IF invariant is source-local THEN use source-native atomic precondition+mutation; harness read-check-write prohibited on that resource UNLESS native mechanism known-weaker (then re-home invariant or add source-side monotonic preconditions)
IF consequential operation returns timeout/connection-loss/indeterminate-error THEN set UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and take no retry/compensation except per R4/R5 UNLESS effect proven naturally idempotent
IF UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and authoritative status path exists THEN reconcile before any retry or compensation UNLESS native idempotency key still validly held (identity-guarded retry may precede)

IF stale concurrent writer would cause material harm THEN achieve exclusion via source-native conditional/monotonic state or fence-capable infrastructure UNLESS the resource itself checks fencing tokens (then lease+fencing acceptable)
decision_rules.activation_condition: material harm from stale concurrent writer
decision_rules.deactivation_condition: never for external SaaS; internal efficiency locks exempt

decision_rules.rule: IF duplicate_harm=MATERIAL AND (no native key OR native window < retention horizon) THEN persist logical-effect identity in HF durable dedup with retention >= horizon, checked before first attempt UNLESS source guarantees unbounded dedup
decision_rules.activation_condition: material duplicate harm, insufficient native coverage
decision_rules.protected_invariant: one effect per identity beyond windows

decision_rules.rule: IF workflow logic may be replayed THEN external effects execute only in non-replayed step/activity boundaries with recorded nondeterminism and stable identity UNLESS effect verified idempotent and harmless on replay
IF effect is NON_IDEMPOTENT_IRREVERSIBLE THEN require approval gate + execution after all fallible/reversible steps UNLESS documented dry-run equivalent exists and is used

IF a step claims compensation support THEN compensation must be a named domain operation with own identity, authorization, idempotency, retry budget >= forward path, and MAY only run on decided-success outcomes UNLESS source-native inverse exists
decision_rules.activation_condition: reversible material step in multi-step flow
decision_rules.deactivation_condition: flow becomes single-transaction at one source

decision_rules.rule: IF an effect executes THEN record attempt/identity/request-evidence/response-ack/authoritative-outcome-evidence as separate fields; never write success from ack alone UNLESS effect is READ_ONLY (attempt log only)
IF a new source/effect is onboarded THEN discover {idempotency key? window? conditional write? status query? dedup semantics?} before first consequential use UNLESS effect is READ_ONLY

IF UNKNOWN_OUTCOME persists past reconciliation deadline AND duplicate_harm=MATERIAL THEN escalate to human with evidence bundle; do not auto-decide UNLESS business rules define bounded auto-policy (e.g., void-after-confirmed-nonexecution)

anti_patterns.name: timeout = failure
anti_patterns.refutation: ack absence is not failure evidence

anti_patterns.name: retry until success
anti_patterns.refutation: unbounded retry without identity duplicates harmful effects

anti_patterns.name: workflow durability = business exactly-once
anti_patterns.refutation: durability covers control state, not external effects

anti_patterns.name: every effect requires an HF ledger
anti_patterns.refutation: reads/natural idempotents need tracing at most; minimality violation
anti_patterns.correct_behavior: identity for harmful non-idempotent class only

anti_patterns.name: distributed lock = safety
anti_patterns.refutation: unfenced locks admit stale writers; leases explicitly unfenced in k8s
anti_patterns.correct_behavior: conditional state transitions / fencing at resources

anti_patterns.name: compensation = rollback
anti_patterns.refutation: compensation is a new forward business operation; can fail or be impossible
anti_patterns.correct_behavior: compensation contracts with authorization and own identity

anti_patterns.name: event sourcing = enterprise maturity
anti_patterns.refutation: ES is a named-requirement tool; audit != event store; durable runtimes use journal/checkpoint internally

anti_patterns.name: current state = known previous effect outcome
anti_patterns.refutation: current state cannot prove previous attempt's outcome

anti_patterns.name: acknowledgement loss = operation failure
anti_patterns.refutation: same evidence as timeout=failure; corrupts messaging-layer designs too

anti_patterns.name: source-native guard duplicated by weaker harness logic
anti_patterns.refutation: weaker checks add failure modes, not strength; protection must live at the resource
anti_patterns.correct_behavior: delegate invariant to source; harness records evidence only

A: effect classification only (READ_ONLY / IDEMPOTENT_WRITE); free retries; request-id tracing; freshness policy for stale-sensitive reads
not applied: effect identity machinery, dedup stores, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME state, locks, compensation, event sourcing
escalation to B on any consequential write
B: EffectContract per consequential effect; native-first delegation (R1, R2, R11); receipts (R10)
identity + durable dedup only where duplicate_harm=MATERIAL and native coverage insufficient (R6)
optimistic versioning on HF-owned state; no leases while single-writer
not applied by default: compensation engine, fencing, ES, harness lock managers
C: Profile B plus — each only under activation condition:
approval gates + pivot-last ordering (R8) for irreversible/privileged effects
compensation contracts with human escalation on compensation failure (R9, R12)
durable dedup with retention >= business horizon (R6)
lease+fencing for HF-internal authority only where conditional transitions cannot replace it (R5); otherwise flow not approvable
integrity-anchored receipt storage when third-party audit required (OQ-6)
explicitly NOT all-mechanisms-enabled: no harness locks, no exactly-once claims, no universal ledger, no mandatory ES, no auto-compensation on unknown outcomes

fault_injection_tests.name: lost acknowledgement
fault_injection_tests.setup: stub source executing write, dropping response; GUARDED/NON_IDEMPOTENT effect
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: state=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; reconcile query issued; single effect
fault_injection_tests.observable_evidence: source effect count=1; state transition log

fault_injection_tests.name: duplicate request
fault_injection_tests.setup: same logical op delivered twice (broker replay)
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: one effect; second suppressed by native key + HF dedup
fault_injection_tests.observable_evidence: dedup hit counter; source effect count

fault_injection_tests.name: crash after external success
fault_injection_tests.setup: kill worker between call OK and record
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: on restart reconcile via identity; adopt outcome; no re-execution
fault_injection_tests.observable_evidence: attempt ledger vs source truth diff = empty

fault_injection_tests.name: concurrent mutation
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: loser receives precondition failure; refreshes; no lost update

fault_injection_tests.name: lease expiry
fault_injection_tests.setup: worker A paused past lease; B acquires
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: A's post-pause writes rejected (conditional/epoch) or A abstains; B reconciles A's in-flights

fault_injection_tests.name: stale worker
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: A's stale write fails at resource; alert raised

fault_injection_tests.name: partial multi-system success
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: A compensated (authorized domain op, idempotent) or forward-recovered per classes; C never started

fault_injection_tests.name: compensation failure
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: retry with own identity; then escalation state + alert; forward state consistent

fault_injection_tests.name: irreversible side effect
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: contract has no compensation field; forward-correction proposal requires approval

fault_injection_tests.name: replay duplication
fault_injection_tests.setup: replay-based runtime; orchestration with external call
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: call not re-issued from replayed logic; activity boundary dedupes via identity

fault_injection_tests.name: delayed duplicate
fault_injection_tests.expected_safe_behavior: HF durable dedup rejects; or source monotonic precondition makes it a no-op
